full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff-respondent No. 1 instituted the suit for declaration of title to 32 a decimals of land appertaining to 13 decimals of plot No. 19452, 13 decimals from plot No. 19368 and 06 1/2 decimals from plot No. 19397 of Mouza Taraf-Umedpur Plaintiffs case in short is that one Ketabdi Monde being the owner in possession settled the suit land with the plaintiffs mother, Orenja Nessa, on 14 Falgun, 1341 B.S. corresponding to 26.2.35 A.D. by a registered patta (Ext. 1) and since then the plaintiffs mother had been possessing the same. After her death the plaintiff inherited the same and has been in possession therein, Defendant No. 1 has been possessing the remaining portion of plot Nos. 19768. 19397. But the suit property has wrongly been recorded in S.A. Khatian No. 868 in the name of the defendants. 

 reversed the decree of the trial court and dismissed the suit holding, inter alia, that the plaintiff failed to prove exclusive possession of Ketab Ali, the plaintiffs mother in the suit land and that the plaintiffs document of title, the certified copy of the patta, Ext. I was not legally proved. In the revision the High Court Division held, inter alia, that the lower appellate court upon misreading of the evidence of P.Ws. 2 and 3 wrongly held that the plaintiff could not prove his possession in the suit land and that the lower appellate court also wrongly held that the plaintiffs document of title i.e. patta was not legally proved. 

 further submits that the High Court Division wrongly held that the certified copy of the original patta proved plaintiffs title to the disputed land while the lower appellate court in consideration of the other relevant facts rightly held that such certified copy was inadmissible in evidence. 

 6. The learned Judge of the High Court Division clearly noticed that the lower appellate court did not consider the entire oral evidence of P.Ws. 2 and 3 and misreading their evidence wrongly held that those two P.Ws supported the plaintiffs possession in only one of the suit plots viz plot NO. 19452 and that they remained silent as regards the plaintiffs possession in the other two plots. The High Court Division found that those two P.Ws specifically stated in their examinations-in-chief as well as in cross-examination that the plaintiff is in possession of the suit property. which is comprised of 32 a decimals of land in total in the three suit plots mentioned above. Non-consideration and misreading of material evidence of the P.Ws being a question of law the High Court Division was justified in setting aside the finding of possession against the plaintiff of the lower appellate court. The High Court Division also rightly repelled the second submission made by Mr. Abdur Rahim as regards the admissibility of Ext. 1, the certified copy of the relevant patta. It was marked as an exhibit without any objection by the defendants. The plaintiff in his evidence also explained the reason for his failure to produce the original patta
